title: A choir of synthesized voices sings a six-part Kyrie, in three versions in one day
summary: On Fri 13 Nov at 14:51Z @yonderdavid.bsky.social (971 followers) posted a video with the text "A little reverb does wonders for them." Its alt text reads: "A choir of Chimera vocal synths sing the Kyrie 1 from Palestrina's Missa Papae Marcelli in six-part harmony." It was posted as a reply to the same maker's falling-block video from that morning and became the maker's most-liked post of the window: 124 likes, 18 reposts, 13 replies, 11 quotes. At 17:31Z @shimmermathlabs.com wondered whether the voices would sound better with a simulated microphone response curve, vocal compressor and tube preamp distortion; at 18:39Z, 68 minutes later, the maker posted a version with "Simulated ribbon microphone curve, tube, and compressor." At 22:23Z the maker posted a third version in which "the voices settle into pure interval ratios when they hold for a while", adding that the voices "now breathe and articulate a little more dynamically, and underwent a bit of vocal training." Asked what comes next, the maker listed vocal folds more like real ones, tuning the high frequencies, and perhaps an instrument simulation. Other members quote-posted the first video with one-line reactions.

made.what: three videos of a synthesized six-voice choir (first version, microphone-chain version, pure-interval version)

couldBeShown: Several synthesized heads singing in six parts; the same passage heard three ways (with reverb; through a simulated ribbon microphone, tube and compressor; with held chords settling into pure interval ratios). The alt text does not say how many heads are on screen or how they are arranged. The show's own voices are synthesized too, so this touches the show's medium.
